# Sampasādanīya Sutta (DN 28 (PTS DN iii 99))

**ID:** DN 28 (PTS DN iii 99)
**Section:** Dīghanikāya (dn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Sampasādanīya Sutta
**PTS:** DN iii 99
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0103m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sampasādanīya Sutta* ("Inspiring Confidence" or "Serene Faith") is the 28th discourse of the *Dīghanikāya* [Walshe 1987]. Set at Pāvārika's Mango Grove in Nālandā, the text depicts Venerable Sāriputta visiting the Buddha shortly before his own passing to proclaim his unshakeable faith in his teacher [Tan 2002]. Sāriputta delivers a "lion's roar" declaring that no ascetic or brahmin has ever been, is, or will be greater or more fully awakened than the Buddha [Tan 2002; Bodhi 2003]. When the Buddha asks whether Sāriputta can read the minds of past, future, or present Buddhas, Sāriputta concedes that he cannot, but explains his certainty through knowledge of the "stream or lineage of the Dhamma" (*dhammanvaya*) [Tan 2002; Norman 1983]. The dialogue expands into an enumeration of the Buddha's unsurpassed excellences (*anuttariya*) regarding spiritual practice, covering topics such as the thirty-seven aids to awakening (*bodhipakkhiyādhammā*), methods of discerning another's state of mind, progressive contemplation of anatomical body parts down to bare bones, classes of liberated persons, and the distinction between defiled "common" superhuman powers (*iddhi*) and the undefiled superhuman power of the noble ones (*ariyā iddhi*) [Norman 1983; Fiordalis 2008; Anālayo 2014; Tan 2008].

 DharmaNexus reports widespread internal Pali text reuse, particularly with AN 3, DN 1, AN 10, AN 4, SN 12, and DN 16, as well as cross-language alignments with the Chinese Āgamas (T 1 and T 99) and Sanskrit texts including the *Saṅghabhedavastu*, *Samādhirājasūtra*, and *Catuṣpariṣatsūtra* [DharmaNexus].
